facility_roles.note: The chamber was built at the University of Chicago and tested in its LASR sub-basement (6 m.w.e.), then installed in the NuMI/MINOS tunnel at Fermilab; the site record is the Fermilab surface campus point, not the tunnel.
facility_roles.quote: Early in 2005 we installed a chamber containing 1.5 kg of CF3 I, an industrial refrigerant commonly used as a fire extinguisher, at the 350-foot depth of the NuMI (Neutrinos at the Main Injector) tunnel in Fermilab.

summary.plain: COUPP-2kg was the first dark-matter bubble chamber of the COUPP team: a small jar of superheated CF3I run in a Fermilab neutrino tunnel from 2005. It proved the technique and set improved limits on WIMPs that couple to nuclear spin.
summary.technical: Room-temperature superheated CF3I bubble chamber (1.5 kg fill, natural-quartz bell jar) installed early in 2005 at the 350-ft level of the NuMI tunnel at Fermilab (the MINOS near-detector hall, 225 m.w.e. per the dissertation). First period: >250 kg-days at up to 80% live fraction and ~1e-10 rejection of photon-induced electrons; improved spin-dependent WIMP-proton limits (Science 319, 933, 2008). Its pressure vessel was reused for COUPP-4kg.
